column1: # Total speakers (first and second language), in millions, of the languages of the benchmark corpora that the source lists.
# Source: Wikipedia, "List of languages by total number of speakers", table "Most spoken languages, Ethnologue, 2026" (figures from
# Read on 2026-11-21. The table lists only languages with 50 million or more total speakers, so the smaller languages of the corpora are not
# in it and are left out of the speaker-weighted figures. The figures are approximate: L2 counts overlap between languages.
# Columns: the language as the benchmark data names it <tab> the total in millions <tab> the entry of the source.
# - Chinese (the Wikipedia corpus) and Chinese (Simplified) and Chinese (Traditional) (the UDHR corpus) are Mandarin text: "Mandarin Chinese".
# - Arabic is Modern Standard Arabic text: "Modern Standard Arabic".
# - Persian is "Iranian Persian"; German is "Standard German".
# - Punjabi is left out: the corpora have it in Gurmukhi (Eastern Punjabi), and the source lists only Western Punjabi.
